name: Subdermal Shear Projector SSP-1 'Faultline'
description: The SSP-1 fires a tightly collimated beam of coherent ultrasonic pressure tuned to the acoustic impedance boundary between biological tissue and subdermal cybernetic plating. The physics are precise and brutal: where natural flesh meets implanted metal, ceramic, or polymer substrate, there exists a discontinuity in acoustic resistance. The Faultline's beam propagates harmlessly through either medium in isolation but generates violent shear stress exactly at that interface. The result is not an explosion or a puncture but a tearing — implants are forcibly separated from the tissue anchoring them, causing catastrophic internal injury without any visible external wound for several seconds.
specifications:
form factor: Rifle configuration, 780mm total length, integrated targeting scope with impedance-mapping overlay
effective range: Up to 60 meters with full effect; degraded performance beyond 80 meters
power source: High-density piezoelectric stack array, 12 shots per module
weight: 3.1 kg
beam frequency: Adaptive, self-tunes to detected implant interface (0.8–2.4 MHz)
effect onset: 2–4 seconds post-impact
wound signature: Internal hemorrhage, implant displacement, no external entry point
module swap time: 4 seconds
tactical_use: The Faultline is used almost exclusively for targeted elimination of high-value augmented individuals in situations where forensic ambiguity is operationally desirable. The delayed wound onset and absence of external trauma create a window in which the target may not realize they have been hit, allowing the shooter to withdraw before the effect becomes apparent. Military applications include anti-cyborg operations where conventional ammunition is defeated by subdermal armor plating — the Faultline bypasses surface hardening entirely by attacking the mounting interface rather than the plating itself.
cultural_context: The SSP-1 is one of the most feared weapons in GLMZ precisely because it is invisible in its operation and insidious in its effect. There is no muzzle flash, no audible report beyond a low hum, and the victim typically dies appearing to have suffered a sudden medical event. Among forensic investigators and corporate security analysts, a Faultline kill is identified by the characteristic 'accordion damage' pattern visible on autopsy imaging — implants displaced centimeters from their original positions, surrounding tissue shredded at the interface. It is almost exclusively associated with state-level actors and the most expensive private military contractors, which means encountering one in a street context signals something has gone deeply wrong with the political order.
known_users: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS black operations units
Anti-augmentation extremist cells with unusual funding
Elite private military contractors on deniable contracts
A known but unnamed fixer called 'The Orthopedist'
story_hooks: A prominent pro-augmentation activist dies of apparent cardiac arrest — but a street-level medic doing the informal autopsy recognizes accordion damage and knows exactly what it means.
A decommissioned ARCTURUS field unit is selling Faultline modules on the black market, and someone needs to find out who their buyer is before the weapon surfaces in a civilian context.
A player character with heavy subdermal plating realizes they are uniquely vulnerable to a weapon they've never had reason to fear before.
The only forensic specialist in GLMZ who can definitively identify a Faultline kill has just been offered a very large sum of money to misattribute cause of death in a high-profile case.

physical_description.visual_profile: A precision rifle with an austere, surgical aesthetic. The body is dominated by a ribbed barrel assembly containing the piezoelectric stack array, flanked by cooling fins that run the weapon's length. The overall silhouette is angular and rectilinear—no curves, no ornamentation. It reads as a tool engineered for a single, terrible purpose.
physical_description.dimensions: 780mm total length, 45mm barrel diameter, 160mm scope rail length. Compact enough for vehicle or close-quarters deployment but undeniably a full rifle platform.
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly light for its size—the piezoelectric stack is dense but compact, and the polymer frame minimizes mass. Feels balanced around the trigger assembly, with slight muzzle-heavy bias from the cooling fins. Manageable in sustained aim, but the weight distribution is unfamiliar to conventional riflemen.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer chassis (carbon-reinforced polycarbonate) with titanium barrel shroud and cooling fin array. Piezoelectric stack visible through service panels along the receiver.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with brushed titanium accents on the barrel and fins. The cooling fins have a subtle heat-anodized bronze patina from operational use. Polymer shows minimal wear—this is a precision weapon kept in strict condition.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary, titanium and bronze secondary, with jet-black grip and rail components. Accent color: faint cyan bioluminescent targeting reticle visible in the scope housing.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer grip with fine knurl pattern for enhanced purchase. The trigger guard is bare titanium, cold to the touch. Charging handle is wrapped in thin para-cord for silent operation.
distinctive_features: Piezoelectric stack array visible through translucent service panel, arranged in concentric rings
Radial cooling fins extending from barrel—functional and intimidating
Integrated targeting scope with cyan-lit impedance-mapping reticle overlay
Modular power cell housing with tool-free quick-swap mechanism at rear stock
No conventional muzzle brake or flash hider—beam emission is silent and invisible
Resonance tuning dial on left side of barrel, marked in MHz increments (0.8–2.4)
Weapon status indicator LEDs (green/amber/red) embedded in the grip
Service placard on right side listing frequency range and tissue/implant impedance values
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS stamped in small block letters on the upper receiver. Serial plate on left side of frame in raised titanium. Smaller warning label on barrel in multiple languages: 'ACOUSTIC DISCONTINUITY PROJECTOR — PROHIBITED CIVILIAN SALE'.
physical_description.condition_typical: Immaculate. This weapon is too rare and too controlled to show field wear. Maintenance records are meticulous. The only evidence of use is faint carbon scoring on the barrel shroud and subtle salt residue around the cooling fins—suggesting deployment in corrosive environments, but nothing more.
